neighbours.label: a military invasion or assault landing (D-Day, amphibious and airborne landings, raids)
fire: On D-Day thousands of Allied soldiers stormed the beaches of Normandy.
The amphibious assault on Iwo Jima began in February 1945.
British commandos carried out a daring raid on the port of Saint-Nazaire.
German paratroopers dropped onto Crete in a massive airborne invasion.
The Marines made an amphibious landing at Inchon behind North Korean lines.
Operation Torch brought American troops ashore in North Africa.
The Doolittle Raid sent bombers over Tokyo in April 1942.
Exiles trained by the CIA landed at the Bay of Pigs in 1961.
quiet: After the war thousands of Allied soldiers returned home from Normandy.
The peace talks over Iwo Jima's future began in February 1952.
British sailors held a quiet memorial service in the port of Saint-Nazaire.
German doctors treated wounded prisoners in a field hospital on Crete.
The Marines held a parade in Inchon years after the armistice.
Wartime convoys shipped food and fuel to depots in England.
American bombers were repaired in hangars in California in April 1942.
Cuban exiles opened restaurants in Miami during the 1960s.
